questions.q:
Assertion (A): A balance with 4 identical packets and a 3-unit weight on the left pan, and 4 of the same packets and a 9-unit weight on the right pan, can be balanced by choosing the right packet weight.
Reason (R): Taking 4 packets off each pan leaves 3 units against 9 units, which are never equal.
questions.a: A is false but R is true.
o: A is false but R is true.
A and R are both true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A and R are both true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.

questions.q: A balance holds 3 identical sacks and a 2-unit weight on one pan and an 11-unit weight on the other. Arjun writes, '3 sacks weigh 11 + 2 = 13, so one sack weighs 13/3.' Is he right? Explain.
questions.a: No. The equation is 3s + 2 = 11, so the 2 must be taken away from both pans: 3s = 11 - 2 = 9, and s = 3. Arjun added 2 instead of removing it. 13/3 does not balance: 3 × 13/3 + 2 = 15, not 11.
s: Gives the verdict that Arjun is wrong
Frames 3s + 2 = 11 and removes 2 from both sides to get s = 3

questions.q:
For Diwali, Sneha lays diya borders with sticks. The first three borders use 8, 13 and 18 sticks, and the pattern keeps growing by the same number of sticks each time. She has 200 sticks in all.
(a) Write an expression for the sticks in border n.
(b) How many sticks does border 12 need?
(c) Which border uses exactly 143 sticks?
(d) She wants to use all 200 sticks in one border. Is that possible? What should she do instead, and why?
questions.a: (a) 5n + 3. (b) 5 × 12 + 3 = 63. (c) 5n + 3 = 143, n = 28. (d) 5n + 3 = 200 gives n = 39.4, not whole, so impossible. Border 39 needs 198 sticks (2 left over); border 40 needs 203, more than she has, so she should build border 39.
s: Part (d): 39.4 not whole, so border 39 with 198 sticks is the best choice

questions.q: A rangoli sequence has 17 dots at Step 4 and 29 dots at Step 7, growing by the same number of dots each step. Meena wants the step that uses exactly 65 dots. Which equation and step are correct?
questions.a: 4n + 1 = 65, so Step 16

questions.q: One matchstick sequence uses 2n + 9 sticks at position n; a second uses 5n - 3 sticks at position n. Both sequences use the same number of sticks at position ___.
Four balances are set up with identical packets of unknown weight. On which balance can the two pans NEVER be made equal by any packet weight?
questions.a: Left: 1 packet and 9 units; right: 6 units
o: Left: 1 packet and 9 units; right: 6 units
Left: 2 packets and 3 units; right: 11 units
Left: 1 packet and 8 units; right: 2 packets and 5 units

questions.q: On a balanced scale the left pan holds one packet of unknown weight p and a 9-unit weight, and the right pan holds only a 4-unit weight. Kabir says, 'The scale will balance if I choose the right packet.' Show that this cannot be true.
questions.a: p + 9 = 4 gives p = 4 - 9 = -5. A packet cannot have a negative weight. Also the left pan already holds 9 units, more than the 4 units on the right, so adding a packet only makes it heavier.
s: Concludes a weight cannot be negative, so it cannot balance

questions.q:
A frieze pattern uses 6n - 2 tiles at position n.
(a) How many tiles does position 9 use?
(b) Gauri claims some position uses exactly 62 tiles. Frame the equation and say whether she can be right.
questions.a: (a) 6 x 9 - 2 = 52 tiles. (b) 6n - 2 = 62 gives 6n = 64 and n = 64/6, about 10.67, which is not a whole position, so no position uses exactly 62 tiles.
s: Part (b): frames 6n - 2 = 62, finds n is not a whole number, so Gauri is wrong

questions.q:
Four statements are written on the board: 3m - 7; 3m - 7 = 11; 9 = 4 + 5; 2k + 1 = k + 8.
(a) Which of them are equations with an unknown to be found?
(b) Solve the one that has the unknown on both sides.
questions.a: (a) 3m - 7 = 11 and 2k + 1 = k + 8. 3m - 7 is only an expression, and 9 = 4 + 5 has no unknown. (b) 2k + 1 = k + 8: take k and 1 from both sides, so k = 7 (check: 15 = 15).
s: Part (a): picks 3m - 7 = 11 and 2k + 1 = k + 8 and rejects the expression and the plain number fact
Part (b): k = 7, checked on both sides

questions.q:
A tile pattern uses 4k + 3 tiles in Step k.
(a) How many tiles are in Step 10?
(b) Frame and solve the equation for a step with 127 tiles.
(c) Find the step with 103 tiles, and say how many steps apart the arrangements with 103 and 127 tiles are. Check against the tile difference.
questions.a: (a) 4 × 10 + 3 = 43. (b) 4k + 3 = 127, 4k = 124, k = 31. (c) 4k + 3 = 103 gives k = 25, so the steps are 31 - 25 = 6 apart; the tiles differ by 127 - 103 = 24 = 4 × 6.

questions.q: Kavya tries whole numbers in 5a - 2 = 2a + 8. At a = 3 the sides are 13 and 14; at a = 4 they are 18 and 16. What does this tell her about the solution?
questions.a: It lies between 3 and 4, because the LHS is smaller at 3 and larger at 4
o: It lies between 3 and 4, because the LHS is smaller at 3 and larger at 4
It is 3, because the two sides are closest there
It is 4, because the LHS has just passed the RHS there
There is none, because no whole number makes the sides equal

questions.q:
An equation is 5q + 8 = 3q + 20.
(a) Describe what is on each pan of the scale it comes from.
(b) Find q, and say which pan is heavier if a packet weighs only 5 units.
questions.a: (a) Left pan: 5 identical packets and an 8-unit weight; right pan: 3 such packets and a 20-unit weight. (b) Remove 3 packets and 8 units from each pan: 2q = 12, q = 6. For q = 5 the left is 33 and the right is 35, so the right pan is heavier.
s: Part (a): names both pans correctly (5 packets + 8 against 3 packets + 20)
Part (b): q = 6, and right pan heavier for q = 5 (33 against 35)

questions.q:
Consider the equation 3x + 2 = x + 14.
Statement 1: At x = 5 the LHS (17) is smaller than the RHS (19).
Statement 2: At x = 7 the LHS is smaller than the RHS.
Statement 3: x = 6 is the solution, because both sides become 20.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: 1 and 3 only

questions.q:
Frame an equation for each situation. Solve (b) and (c).
(a) Five identical stones balance a 35-unit weight.
(b) One stone and a 12-unit weight balance three of the same stones.
(c) The matchstick arrangement at position n uses 2n + 1 sticks, and one arrangement has 71 sticks.
s: Part (b): solves s = 6 (removing one stone from both pans)

questions.q:
A sweet-shop scale balances 5 identical laddus and a 40 g wrapper against a 190 g weight.
(a) Frame the equation, taking one laddu as l grams.
(b) Use the LHS to show that l = 20 does not balance the scale, and then find the right value of l.
questions.a: (a) 5l + 40 = 190. (b) For l = 20 the LHS is 5 x 20 + 40 = 140, which is not 190. Removing 40 from both pans gives 5l = 150, so l = 30 g.
s: Part (b): LHS 140 for l = 20 fails; l = 30

questions.q: Compare the equations 6x - 4 = 20 and 20 = 6x - 4. Name the LHS of each, and say, with the value, whether they have the same solution.
questions.a: In the first, the LHS is 6x - 4 and the RHS is 20; in the second, the LHS is 20 and the RHS is 6x - 4. Both have the solution x = 4 (6 x 4 - 4 = 20), since swapping the sides keeps the equality.
s: Names the LHS of each equation correctly (6x - 4 and 20)
Finds x = 4 for both and says swapping sides keeps the solution

questions.q: On a balanced scale, the left pan holds 3 identical packets and a 4-unit weight, and the right pan holds one such packet and a 10-unit weight. What does one packet weigh?
questions.a: 3 units

questions.q:
A grain merchant in Nashik balances rice sacks on a scale. The left pan holds 3 identical sacks and a 2 kg weight. The right pan holds 1 such sack and a 14 kg weight. The scale is exactly balanced. His van has a load limit of 140 kg of sacks.
(a) Frame the equation, calling the weight of a sack s kg.
(b) Which equal things can be removed from both pans to leave sacks only on one pan, and what equation is left?
(c) Find the weight of a sack.
(d) He wants to load 25 such sacks. Does the load stay within the limit? Give a reason.
questions.a: (a) 3s + 2 = s + 14. (b) Remove one sack and 2 kg from each pan, leaving 2s = 12. (c) s = 6 kg. (d) 25 × 6 = 150 kg, which is more than 140 kg, so no.
s: Part (b): removes one sack and 2 kg from both pans, 2s = 12

questions.q: Write a short story (a real-life situation) that can be described by the equation 6 + 3p = 27, and say what p stands for.
questions.a: Example: A tailor buys 3 identical buttons packets and a 6-rupee thread reel; the total is ₹27; p is the price of one packet (p = 7). Any consistent story with a fixed amount 6, three equal unknown parts p and total 27 is accepted.
s: Story includes a fixed part 6 and three equal unknown parts
Total is 27 and the story agrees with the equation

questions.q: A row of n matchstick squares in a chain needs 4 sticks for the first square and 3 more for each extra square. Jasmine has exactly 91 sticks. How many squares can she make using all of them?
questions.a: 30 squares

questions.a: 513, because 36 is 4 times 9, so both sides are divided by 4
o: 513, because 36 is 4 times 9, so both sides are divided by 4
2043, because 36 - 9 is subtracted from both sides
1026, because both sides are divided by 2

questions.q: Sunil starts from 24 + 18 = 42. He writes 24 + 18 - 6 = 42 + 6 and says he has kept the equality. What is wrong with his working?
questions.a: He took 6 from the left but added 6 to the right, giving 36 and 48
o: He took 6 from the left but added 6 to the right, giving 36 and 48
He should have divided both sides by 6 and not subtracted anything
Taking a number away from a true statement always makes it false
He should have taken 6 away from the right side alone and left the left alone

questions.q: True or False: since 24 x 15 x 6 = 2160, the value of 24 x 15 is 2160 - 6 = 2154.
questions.a: False. Subtracting 6 does not undo multiplying by 6; the inverse of multiplying by 6 is dividing by 6, applied to both sides. So 24 x 15 = 2160 / 6 = 360 (check: 24 x 15 = 360).
s: Reason: division, not subtraction, undoes multiplication; the correct value is 360

questions.q: Make up your own problem: give a product of five whole numbers and its value, and ask for the product of any four of those numbers without multiplying. Write the answer and the method.
questions.a: Example: 6 x 7 x 13 x 5 x 4 = 10920. Find 6 x 7 x 13 x 5. Divide both sides by 4 (multiplication and division are inverse operations): 10920 / 4 = 2730. Any correct problem with a matching key is accepted.
s: Gives five factors with their correct product
Asks for the product of four of them, with the right value
Names the operation done on both sides and why it is allowed

questions.q: Tanvi tries whole numbers in 7x - 5 = 12. At x = 2 the LHS is 9 and at x = 3 the LHS is 16. What can she conclude?
questions.a: The solution lies between 2 and 3, so it is not a whole number
o: The solution lies between 2 and 3, so it is not a whole number
x = 2 is the solution because 9 is the closest to 12
The equation has no solution because neither try gives 12

questions.q:
In a Class 7 maths club contest at a Pune school, three students try values in the equation 4x - 7 = 57. Ananya tries x = 10, Bilal tries x = 15 and Charu tries x = 18. In the final round the equation is 8x - 14 = 114. Charu says, 'The numbers are about twice as big, so x will be about 32.'
(a) Find the LHS for each student's value of 4x - 7, and say who is closest to 57 and by how much.
(b) Between which two tried values does the solution lie?
(c) Solve 4x - 7 = 57 by doing the same operation on both sides.
(d) Is Charu right about the final round? Judge her claim without solving the final equation from scratch, and give the reason.
questions.a: (a) 33, 53, 65; Bilal is closest, 4 below 57. (b) Between 15 and 18 (53 is below 57 and 65 is above). (c) 4x = 64, x = 16. (d) No. 8x - 14 = 2(4x - 7) and 114 = 2 x 57, so the final equation is the contest equation with both sides multiplied by 2; the same operation on both sides keeps the solution, so x is still 16, not 32.
s: Part (a): 33, 53 and 65, with Bilal closest by 4
Part (d): Charu is wrong; both sides are doubled so x stays 16

questions.q: Arjun solves 7n - 12 = 100 by trials. At n = 10 the LHS is 58 and each increase of n by 1 raises the LHS by 7. Which next trial gives exactly 100?

Seema solves 8m + 3 = 515 by trials. At m = 50 the LHS is 403 and at m = 100 it is 803.
(a) Between which two of her trials does the solution lie, and why?
(b) Use inverse operations on the equation to find m exactly.
questions.a: (a) Between 50 and 100, because the LHS rises with m and 403 is below 515 while 803 is above it. (b) Subtract 3 from both sides: 8m = 512, then divide by 8: m = 64 (check: 8 x 64 + 3 = 515).
s: Part (a): between 50 and 100, with the reason that 403 < 515 < 803

questions.q: Rohit says n = 7 solves 4n - 3 = 22 and n = 5 solves it too. Show that neither is a solution, and say between which whole numbers the true solution lies.
questions.a: n = 5 gives 4(5) - 3 = 17 and n = 7 gives 4(7) - 3 = 25; neither is 22. The LHS grows with n, 17 is below 22 and 25 above it, so the solution lies between 5 and 7 (it is 25/4, between 6 and 7, because n = 6 gives 21).
s: LHS 17 for n = 5 and 25 for n = 7
Says the solution lies between 5 and 7 and is not a whole number

questions.q:
Rahul solves 5n - 3 = 142 by trials and records the LHS as 47 at n = 10, 97 at n = 20 and 147 at n = 30.
(a) Between which two trials does the solution lie?
(b) The LHS rises by 5 for every step of n. Use this to say how many steps back from n = 30 reach 142, and name n.
questions.a: (a) Between n = 20 and n = 30, since 97 < 142 < 147. (b) 147 is 5 more than 142, which is one step of n, so n = 29 (check: 5 x 29 - 3 = 142).
s: Part (a): between 20 and 30 with the comparison 97 < 142 < 147
Part (b): one step back, n = 29, checked

questions.q: Meera says, 'Doing the same thing to both sides of 15 + 8 = 23 keeps the equality when we add or subtract, but multiplying can break it.' Is she fully right? Test multiplication by 4.
questions.a: She is right about adding and subtracting but wrong about multiplying. Multiplying both sides by 4 gives (15 + 8) × 4 = 92 and 23 × 4 = 92, still equal. Dividing also keeps equality.
s: Says she is partly right: add and subtract keep equality
States that multiplication and division also keep the equality

questions.q: A number is multiplied by 4 and then 6 is added, giving 50. Arjun undoes this by subtracting 6 and then dividing by 4. Bina divides 50 by 4 and then subtracts 6. Whose order is correct, and what is the number?
questions.a: Arjun's order, giving 11

questions.q:
Priti solves 100 - 3n = 46 by trials.
(a) Find the LHS at n = 10 and at n = 20.
(b) The LHS falls as n grows. Decide whether the solution lies above or below n = 20 and find it.
questions.a: (a) 100 - 30 = 70 and 100 - 60 = 40. (b) 46 lies between 40 and 70, so n lies between 10 and 20, below 20 because the LHS falls as n rises. Then 3n = 100 - 46 = 54 and n = 18.
s: Part (b): solution between 10 and 20 (below 20) and n = 18

questions.q:
Solve 3x + 5 = 50 in two ways.
(a) Use trial and error with at least three trials, showing the LHS each time.
(b) Solve it again by doing the same operation on both sides.
(c) Which method would you prefer for 3x + 5 = 51, and why?
questions.a: (a) x = 10 gives 35, x = 20 gives 65, x = 15 gives 50, so x = 15. (b) 3x = 45, x = 15. (c) The second: 51 gives 3x = 46 and x = 46/3, which no whole-number trial can find.
s: Part (a): three trials with correct LHS values
Part (b): subtracts 5 from both sides to get 3x = 45
Part (b): divides by 3 to get x = 15
Part (c): chooses the systematic method with the reason

questions.q: Only one of these equations has a whole-number solution, so only it can be solved exactly by whole-number trial and error. Which one?

It is known that (5/7) × 21 × 14 × (3/4) = 315/2. Find (5/7) × 21 × 14 without multiplying it out.
(a) What do you do to both sides?
(b) Carry it out.
(c) Check your result by direct multiplication and say why the first method is allowed.
questions.a: (a) Divide both sides by 3/4, which means multiplying by 4/3. (b) (315/2) × (4/3) = 210. (c) Directly: (5/7) × 21 = 15 and 15 × 14 = 210. It is allowed because the same operation on both sides keeps the equality and division undoes multiplication.
s: Part (c): justifies with inverse operations and equality kept

questions.q:
To solve 8x - 3 = 61, Ria subtracts 3 from both sides and Sam adds 3 to both sides.
(a) Whose first step is correct, and why?
(b) Complete the solution.
questions.a: (a) Sam's: the term -3 is undone by adding 3 to both sides; subtracting 3 would give 8x - 6 = 58. (b) 8x = 64, so x = 8 (check: 8 x 8 - 3 = 61).
s: Part (a): Sam's step, because adding 3 undoes subtracting 3

questions.q:
Consider the equation 5n - 4 = 36.
Statement 1: Since 5 x 7 - 4 = 31 and 5 x 9 - 4 = 41, the solution is either 7 or 9.
Statement 2: The solution is 8, because 5 x 8 - 4 = 36.
Statement 3: Adding 4 to both sides and then dividing both sides by 5 gives the same value, 8.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: 2 and 3 only

questions.q:
Bhavna's savings jar holds ₹110. She puts in ₹30 at the end of every month and wants to buy a school bag costing ₹350.
(a) Write an expression for the money in the jar after m months.
(b) Frame the equation for the bag's price and try m = 5 to see how far she is.
(c) Find, by any method, the month in which the jar holds exactly ₹350.
(d) On the day she reaches exactly ₹350, the shop raises the price of that bag to ₹380, but a plainer bag at ₹330 is still on sale. Should she buy the plainer bag at once or wait for the ₹380 bag? Decide, using numbers from your answers.
questions.a: (a) 110 + 30m. (b) 110 + 30m = 350; m = 5 gives 260, still 90 short. (c) 30m = 240, m = 8. (d) Either choice is accepted if the numbers back it. Buying the ₹330 bag now leaves her ₹20 and no wait. Waiting costs one more month: 110 + 30 x 9 = 380 gives exactly the new price, so she gets the better bag but only after another month and with nothing left over.
s: Part (b): frames 110 + 30m = 350 and finds 260 at m = 5
Part (d): a justified choice using 350 - 330 = 20 left over or 110 + 30 x 9 = 380 (one more month)

s: Part (b): collects on the right, reaches 4k = 18 and the same k, 9/2

questions.q: Ravi must solve 24(x + 3) + 60 = 300. He notices that 24, 60 and 300 are all divisible by 12. What simpler equation can he use?
questions.a: Divide both sides by 12: 2(x + 3) + 5 = 25

questions.q:
The prize money of the Class 7 science fair was shared equally among 12 group members and each member received ₹45. The group now thinks of letting members step back, so the same total is shared equally among the rest. Everyone must receive a whole number of rupees, and any rupees left over go to the school library.
(a) Frame an equation for the total amount m and solve it.
(b) If 2 members step back and 10 share the total, how much does each get and how much is left?
(c) If only 1 member steps back and 11 share it, how much does each get and how much is left?
(d) The group can choose either plan. Compare the two plans using your answers and decide, giving a reason.
questions.a: (a) m/12 = 45, m = 540. (b) 540/10 = ₹54 each, nothing left. (c) 540 = 11 x 49 + 1, so ₹49 each and ₹1 left for the library. (d) Either choice is accepted if the numbers back it. 10 members: each gains ₹9 over ₹45, nothing is left, but 2 members receive nothing. 11 members: each gains only ₹4, ₹1 goes to the library, but only 1 member is left out.
s: Part (d): a decision backed by the gains (₹9 against ₹4) and the members left out (2 against 1)

questions.q:
Match each equation in Column I with its solution in Column II.
Column I: 1. 3(x - 2) = 15   2. 4m - 9 = m + 9   3. u/5 + 2 = 6   4. 12 - 2w = 4
Column II: A. 20   B. 4   C. 7   D. 6

Teena says, 'In 3(x - 2) = 15 I can divide both sides by 3 first or expand the bracket first, and both give x = 7. Dividing first works only because 15 is a multiple of 3; for 3(x - 2) = 16 I must expand.' Is she fully right? Test both of her statements.
questions.a: Partly right. For 3(x - 2) = 15 both ways give x = 7 (x - 2 = 5, or 3x - 6 = 15, 3x = 21). But dividing first is also allowed for 3(x - 2) = 16: x - 2 = 16/3 so x = 22/3, and expanding gives 3x - 6 = 16, 3x = 22, x = 22/3. A multiple of 3 is not needed, because dividing both sides by 3 is always an equal operation.
s: Confirms that both ways give x = 7 for 3(x - 2) = 15
Tests 3(x - 2) = 16 by both ways and gets x = 22/3 each time
Verdict: partly right, since dividing first needs no multiple of 3

questions.q:
Three students solved 6y - 5 = 2y + 19 and got different answers. Anil got y = 6. Beena wrote 6y + 2y = 19 + 5 and got y = 3. Chitra wrote 6y - 2y = 19 - 5 and got y = 7/2. In the exam, a student has time for only one extra step at the end: either substitute her answer in the original equation, or redo the whole solution.
(a) Solve the equation correctly.
(b) Check Beena's answer by substituting it in both sides.
(c) What exact slip did Chitra make?
(d) Which extra step should a student choose, and why?
questions.a: (a) 4y = 24, y = 6. (b) LHS = 6(3) - 5 = 13; RHS = 2(3) + 19 = 25; they differ, so y = 3 is wrong. (c) She wrote 19 - 5 on the right instead of 19 + 5 (moving -5 across should give +5). (d) Substitute: it takes two quick multiplications, exposes both slips as unequal sides (as in (b)), whereas redoing the work may repeat the same habit.
s: Part (d): chooses substitution with the reason

questions.q:
Solve 6x - 14 = 40.
(a) State the first step and the equation it gives.
(b) Find x and check it in the original equation.
questions.a: (a) Add 14 to both sides: 6x = 54. (b) x = 9; check 6(9) - 14 = 40, equal to the RHS.
s: Part (a): adds 14 to both sides to get 6x = 54

questions.q:
Mira solves -6w = -15 and writes w = 5/2. Poorva says the answer must be -5/2 because the coefficient -6 is negative.
(a) Test both answers in the equation.
(b) State who is right and why.
questions.a: (a) -6 x 5/2 = -15, which matches the RHS; -6 x (-5/2) = 15, which does not. (b) Mira is right: dividing -15 by -6 gives a positive 15/6 = 5/2; the sign of the answer comes from dividing two negatives, not from the sign of the coefficient alone.
s: Part (b): Mira is right, since a negative divided by a negative is positive

s: Part (d): 52 is above the largest possible answer 50

questions.a: (a) 200 + 50s = 300 + 50s, which leads to 200 = 300, false. (b) They are never equal; X is always ₹100 cheaper. (c) 200 + 50s = 300 + 45s, 5s = 100, s = 20. X is the safer advice, since she is sure of 15 sessions and Y saves only ₹20 even if she reaches 24; Y is acceptable if she is confident of 24. A justified choice earns the mark.
s: Part (b): never equal; X is always ₹100 cheaper
Part (d): fees at 15 and 24 sessions computed (950 v 975, 1400 v 1380) and a choice justified by them

A trick: think of a number, add 6, multiply by 4, subtract 4 times the number you started with, then divide by 8. The answer is always 3.

questions.a: (a) x; x + 6; 4x + 24; 24; 3. (b) After multiplying, 4x + 24; subtracting 4x removes the unknown and leaves 24, and 24 ÷ 8 = 3 for every x. (c) Think of x, multiply by 5, add 15, divide by 5, subtract x, add 4: (5x + 15)/5 - x + 4 = x + 3 - x + 4 = 7.
s: Part (b): the x cancels so the result is always 3
Part (c): designs a trick with steps

questions.a: Partly right. Multiplying both sides of n + 2 = 9 by 6 gives 6n + 12 = 54, and n = 7 satisfies it (42 + 12 = 54). But 6n + 2 = 54 multiplies only the n and not the 2, so it is not the same operation on both sides; it gives 6n = 52, n = 26/3, and n = 7 does not satisfy it (42 + 2 = 44).

(b) Write the equation that step (3) gives.
(c) Test u = 6 in both groups' final equations.

questions.a: (a) 5u = 30, then 5u - 8 = 22. (b) 6u - 8 = 22 + u. (c) P: 36 - 8 = 28 and 22 + 6 = 28, equal. Q: 28 and 23 + 6 = 29, unequal. (d) Group P wins. Q wrote 23 instead of 22, so its equation 6u - 8 = 23 + u gives 5u = 31, u = 31/5 = 6.2, not 6.
s: Part (c): P gives 28 and 28; Q gives 28 and 29
Part (d): P wins; Q's equation has the solution 31/5 = 6.2

In a Chennai apartment, overhead Tank A holds 300 litres and gains 45 litres every minute. Tank B holds 1200 litres and gains 15 litres every minute. Each tank overflows at 2000 litres. The caretaker can go up to the roof only once, at the 40th minute, and compares the tanks using Brahmagupta's formula.

(b) Use the formula to find when A and B hold the same amount.
(c) Check by finding the amount in each tank at that time, and also at the 40th minute.
(d) Is a single visit at the 40th minute safe? If not, find the latest whole minute at which one visit still catches both tanks before overflow.
questions.a: (a) 45t + 300 = 15t + 1200. (b) t = (1200 - 300) ÷ (45 - 15) = 30. (c) At 30 minutes both hold 1650 litres. At 40 minutes A holds 300 + 1800 = 2100 and B holds 1200 + 600 = 1800 litres. (d) No: Tank A has already passed 2000 (it fills at 300 + 45t = 2000, t about 37.8). The latest whole minute is 37, when A holds 1965 litres (minute 38 gives 2010); B is far from full.
s: Part (c): 1650 each at 30 minutes; 2100 and 1800 at 40 minutes
